name: Chameleon
description: Nanocrystal lattices tune wavelength reflection through structural color. Each eye moves independently with 360-degree field, processing two visual streams simultaneously. Ballistic tongue reaches 41g in 20ms. Split-brain visual processing.

core_attributes.neurology: independent bilateral visual processing, rapid motor cortex
core_attributes.pattern: structural nanocrystal color, independent eye tracking, ballistic predation, parallel perception

scope.definition: Fraction of visible spectrum chromatophore color shift achievable via guanine nanocrystal lattice tuning alone (without pigment cell contribution), measured in isolated iridophore cell preparations.

evidence.source: Teyssier et al. (2015) 'Photonic crystals cause active colour change in chameleons', Nature Communications 6:6368.
cross_domain_examples: panther chameleon S/M nanocrystal lattice shifts peak wavelength 300-750 nm via mechanical stretch
morpho butterfly wing iridescence: static structural color from same photonic crystal principle
cephalopod iridophore cells use same tunable nanocrystal mechanism for dynamic color

scope.falsifiability: If isolated chameleon iridophore cells show no spectral shift under mechanical deformation, nanocrystal lattice tuning is not the color-change mechanism.
scope.measurement_limits: Nanocrystal mechanism explains rapid (1-2 s) color change. Slow hormonal pigment dispersal adds additional color range on 5-30 min timescale. Both mechanisms co-occur.

scope.definition: Angular range (degrees) over which each chameleon eye can independently rotate on horizontal and vertical axes simultaneously, measured via high-speed video in awake restrained subjects.

evidence.source: Ott & Schaeffel (1995) 'A negatively powered lens in the chameleon', Nature 373:692-694; Pettigrew et al. (1999) chameleon eye movement analysis.
cross_domain_examples: each chameleon eye rotates ±90° horizontal, ±60° vertical independently — 180° monocular field
foveation switch: binocular convergence for prey strike within 0.1 s from monocular scanning
mantis shrimp eyes: analogous independent eye movement for extended visual field coverage

scope.falsifiability: If chameleon eyes are shown to be mechanically coupled during scanning (not truly independent), the 360° combined field model is incorrect.
scope.measurement_limits: Independent tracking is interrupted during prey capture — eyes converge for binocular depth estimation. Speed of independent movement slows in cold conditions (<15°C).

scope.definition: Accuracy (fraction of strikes landing within 1 tongue-length of target center) for Jackson's chameleon tongue projection at distances 1-1.5× body length, measured with high-speed camera.

evidence.source: Wainwright et al. (2000) 'The force velocity trade-off in ballistic tongue projection', American Zoologist 40:1099; de Groot & van Leeuwen (2004) chameleon tongue ballistics, Journal of Experimental Biology.
cross_domain_examples: ballistic tongue acceleration 500 m/s² — highest acceleration in any tetrapod appendage
strike accuracy 0.88 at 1× body length, 0.74 at 2× body length
frog tongue uses hydrogel adhesion and different ballistic architecture — convergent rapid-capture strategy

scope.falsifiability: If strike accuracy is measured below 0.70 at standard 1× body length distance in healthy subjects, the ballistic projection model overstates precision.
scope.measurement_limits: Accuracy degrades significantly beyond 1.5× body length. Cold-blooded: tongue speed and accuracy decline sharply below 20°C. Prey size relative to tongue pad affects adhesion success.
